data.title: bn-tnk: M1.5.1 Claim template and slot resolution for `web-authz/private-object-read`
data.description: Compiled scourge.claim-template.v1 registry and pure Templates.resolve for web-authz/private-object-read. Property slots are operator-only (SLOT_CONFLICT before any effect); the generic INV-37 guard refuses a non-GET/HEAD resolved read selector (METHOD_REFUSED); the experiment digest binds every frozen field and no per-run canary or nonce. Pure module: no network, process, adapter, credential, target interaction or dispatch.

data.body:
FINDING (low, contract conformance, BLOCKING): `ref_name` parsing is not the frozen pattern, and the tail beyond the fifth dot-segment is not validated at all.

Where: `valid_ref_name` (crates/scourge-core/src/template/mod.rs:152-164). It validates at most five dotted parts with `parts.by_ref().take(5).all(..)` and never checks that the iterator is exhausted. `declaration::registered_ref` gets this right with a trailing `parts.next().is_none()`; this copy dropped it.

Frozen contract: `schemas/claim-template.v1.schema.json` -> `$defs/ref_name` = `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(?:\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}){0,4}$`, i.e. at most 5 parts.

Accepted but schema-invalid (verified against the exact parser with an independent harness outside the tree):
- `a.b.c.d.e.f` and `a.b.c.d.e.f.g.h` (too many parts)
- `a.b.c.d.e.f.GET /admin` and `a.b.c.d.e.f.https://attacker.example/x` (the 7th part is never tested, so arbitrary text passes as a `StepId`/`ControlId`)

Reach: `recipe[].id`, `recipe[].controls`, `controls` map keys, `controls[].step`, `cleanup.step`, `retest_variants[].step`.

Why it matters even though it is low: it is over-acceptance only, the text is inert here (no request grammar, no dispatch, nothing is sent) and templates are compiled, so nothing exploitable follows today. But (a) the bone's M0.7 acceptance says "validate and instantiate the exact `scourge.claim-template.v1`", which this is not; (b) INV-44's premise is that every reader agrees on one interpretation, and `just schema-check` (jsonschema) and this parser now disagree about which templates are valid; (c) `StepId` is the value M1.5 will write into the verification record as `round[].flows[].step` (ADR cross-lane-contracts: "name the recipe step for every flow"), so a request-line-shaped identifier would reach retained evidence. It becomes a concrete defect the moment a second template is compiled and the flow writer lands.

Reproduce: `ClaimTemplate::parse_json` on the frozen example with `recipe[0].id` set to `a.b.c.d.e.f.GET /admin` returns `Ok`; `re.match(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(?:\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}){0,4}$", "a.b.c.d.e.f.GET /admin")` is `None`.

Fix: require exhaustiveness after the five-part check (`&& parts.next().is_none()`), and add negative parse tests for a 6-part step id, a 6-part control key and a 7-part id with a request-shaped tail. Worth adding a fixture-driven cross-check so the Rust matchers and the frozen schema cannot drift again.

FINDING (low, contract conformance, BLOCKING): `reason_code` accepts lengths the frozen schema rejects.

Where: `Control.reason_code` (crates/scourge-core/src/template/mod.rs:275) is a `wire::ReasonCode`. That type (crates/scourge-core/src/wire.rs:79-84) checks only "starts uppercase, remaining bytes in `[A-Z0-9_]`" and applies no length bound.

Frozen contract: `$defs/reason_code` = `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{1,63}$`, i.e. minimum 2 characters, maximum 64.

Accepted but schema-invalid: `"A"` (1 char) and a 65-character code, in `controls.*.reason_code`. Verified against the exact parser with an independent harness.

Why it matters even though it is low: over-acceptance only, the value is inert, and the shipped fixture and the frozen oracle registry only use codes inside the bound, so nothing exploits it today. But a control's `reason_code` is the code the verifier emits when a control fails (`reason_codes[]` in the record); a template declaring an out-of-bound code would be shape-valid to the verifier and invalid to `just schema-check`, which is the contract-boundary disagreement INV-44 exists to prevent.

Note the defect lives in `wire.rs`, outside this diff: this commit is the first consumer that has a frozen length bound for the type, so it is fair to fix here (bound the check locally with a template-owned reason-code type, or tighten `ReasonCode` itself with `(2..=64).contains(&value.len())` and re-run the oracle-contract checks).

Fix: enforce the `{1,63}` suffix bound and add negative tests for a 1-character and a 65-character reason code.

NON-BLOCKING observations from the security review (verified correct in substance; recorded so they are not lost before M1.5/M1.6).

1. Verified-correct core. Property slots are operator-only from the channel, not from the value: `check_supplier` runs before property resolution for both `lead_slots` and `overrides`, so a lead that repeats the operator's exact operation, claims an operator supplier, or an operator `--slot read=...`, is `SLOT_CONFLICT` (exit 2) before any effect. The declared property fixes the operations; the lead only selects a declared label. Engagement revision and digest must both match the accepted manifest. 49-field digest mutation matrix, canary/nonce exclusion, deterministic ordering, frozen code/exit mapping and the INV-37 method guard all reproduce independently.

2. Future-template slot typing (latent, no exposure in this commit). `SlotKind::Policy|Observation|Artifact|Selector` slots other than a slot literally named `read` are bound to raw `WireText` with no validation. The shipped template has no such slot, so nothing is reachable today, but a future template that lets a lead supply one would freeze lead-authored arbitrary text (URL-shaped, header-shaped) into the experiment digest and the retained artifact. Suggest validating any non-principal lead-supplied slot against a registered-reference or `Prose`-like type when the second template lands, and keying INV-37 on the recipe's read operation rather than on the literal slot name `read`.

3. Digest scope for the compiled template. The experiment binds `template.id` + `template.version`, not the template content, so a silently altered compiled recipe that keeps version 1 keeps the same digest. That matches plan section 8 ("binds ... template version") and the ADR, so it is not a defect; if you later want tamper-evidence for the compiled registry, add a template digest to the experiment.

4. Precedence nuance for the M1.6.4 acceptance. A lead that supplies the same property slot twice gets `INPUT_AMBIGUOUS` (exit 3) rather than `SLOT_CONFLICT` (exit 2), because duplicate detection precedes the supplier check. Both are typed refusals before traffic and the docs make duplicate input `INPUT_AMBIGUOUS`, so this looks intended; flagging it only because F-38/M1.6.4 phrasing ("any lead-supplied read/plant/remove is SLOT_CONFLICT") reads narrower, and a future test that asserts the code for a duplicated property slot should expect `INPUT_AMBIGUOUS`.

5. `Templates::resolve_in` is private, so the generic INV-37 guard is only exercisable in-crate. Fine by design (compiled registry, no loader), but it means no external cross-check can construct a second template; if that matters, expose a sealed test-only constructor rather than a public registry mutator.

data.body:
Fixed at 143d4ce03f51582fcd4a49e691aaf84d8005909c (base 4d10a8338e2321a23155cf55c11443f9feffec4e), workspace bn-tnk.

Change: valid_ref_name (crates/scourge-core/src/template/mod.rs:159) now validates the first segment, then iterates the remaining split to exhaustion: every further segment must be 1..=32 bytes and [a-z][a-z0-9_]*, and a fifth further segment is refused outright. There is no tail the loop skips, so the sixth, seventh, eighth segment and any request- or URL-shaped suffix are declaration errors. The first segment stays unbounded, matching $defs/ref_name.

Drift guard you suggested: tests read the pattern itself from schemas/claim-template.v1.schema.json (tests.rs:560 frozen_pattern translates Python's (?![\s\S]) end guard to Rust's $, since Rust regex has no lookaround) and compare it with StepId/ControlId over a 28-candidate matrix plus every segment count 0..=8 (tests.rs:624). The matrix covers a.b.c.d.e.f / .g / .g.h, a.b.c.d.e.f.GET /admin, a.b.c.d.e.f.https://attacker.example/x, a bad sixth segment, empty segments, 32/33-byte segments, non-ASCII, hyphens, leading dots and trailing newlines.

Negative parse tests at every ref_name position (tests.rs:690, 6 positions x 8 values = 48 cases): recipe[].id, recipe[].controls[], controls map key, controls[].step, cleanup.step, retest_variants[].step, each with 6/7/8 well-formed parts, request-shaped and URL-shaped sixth segments, and a non-conforming sixth segment. Maximum-valid boundary at tests.rs:653: five segments whose four dotted parts are exactly 32 bytes (133 bytes) is accepted by the type and by a document that parses and validates; one byte over in each dotted position is refused.

Independent schema-differential matrix: 63 documents (baseline + 10 ref values x 6 positions + 8 reason-code values) judged twice - by scripts/check-schema-contracts.py check_shape over the frozen schema, and by the real ClaimTemplate::parse_json. At 143d4ce: 63/63 agree. At c40a599 (pre-fix) the same matrix reports 38 mismatches, all of them schema-invalid documents the old parser accepted (6/7/8 parts, request/URL tails and a bad sixth segment across all 6 positions, plus the two reason-code lengths in the sibling finding).

Evidence: 37 template tests pass (31 preserved + 6 new; 5 of the 6 fail at c40a599), 53 scourge-core lib tests, 120 scourge-verify tests, cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -D warnings, cargo doc, and full just check exit 0 (TMPDIR=/tmp/tt).

Review retargeted to 143d4ce, votes cleared, re-review requested. Not approved, merged, closed, pushed or claim-released.

Fixed at 143d4ce03f51582fcd4a49e691aaf84d8005909c (base 4d10a8338e2321a23155cf55c11443f9feffec4e), workspace bn-tnk.

Change: tightened the shared wire type rather than forking a template-owned copy. ReasonCode (crates/scourge-core/src/wire.rs:79-93) now requires 2..=64 bytes (the {1,63} suffix bound) in addition to the existing uppercase-lead and [A-Z0-9_]-only alphabet, i.e. exactly ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{1,63}$ / $defs/reason_code. Control.reason_code (template/mod.rs:288) therefore refuses "A" and a 65-byte code at parse time, before validate().

No regression in the oracle reasons: every frozen code in docs/contracts/oracle-specifications.v1.json is inside the bound - CANARY_NOT_SPECIFIC, EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE, OBSERVER_INVALID, OWNER_VIEW_LOST, SAME_SUBJECT, SESSION_DRIFT (flows[].failure_code plus predicate.invalid_precedence and invalid_reasons) - and tests.rs:805 reads that file and asserts every one is accepted by the tightened type, so a future out-of-bound code fails the build instead of the runtime expect. scourge-verify's ReasonCode::from_str call sites all pass.

Tests: tests.rs:720 reason_codes_are_exactly_the_frozen_bounds compares ReasonCode with the pattern read from schemas/claim-template.v1.schema.json over 82 candidates (every length 0..=70, empty, lowercase, digit-lead, underscore-lead, hyphen, space, trailing newline, non-ASCII): explicit 1-byte rejection, 65-byte rejection, 2-byte acceptance and 64-byte acceptance. tests.rs:768 template_controls_reject_reason_codes_outside_the_frozen_bound does the same through ClaimTemplate::parse_json and validate() on the frozen example: 2, 64 and SAME_SUBJECT parse and validate, 1, lowercase and 65 are declaration errors.

Evidence: 37 template tests (5 of the 6 new ones fail at c40a599), 53 scourge-core lib tests, 120 scourge-verify tests, 63/63 agreement in the independent schema-differential matrix, cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -D warnings, cargo doc, full just check exit 0 (TMPDIR=/tmp/tt).

Review retargeted to 143d4ce, votes cleared, re-review requested. Not approved, merged, closed, pushed or claim-released.

Acknowledged at 143d4ce03f51582fcd4a49e691aaf84d8005909c (base 4d10a83); recording the disposition of the five non-blocking observations. None is closed by this commit, and none is contradicted by it.

1. Verified-correct core (operator-only property slots from the channel, SLOT_CONFLICT before effect, engagement revision+digest pin, INV-37 GET/HEAD guard, frozen code/exit mapping, 49-field digest with canary/nonce excluded, deterministic ordering): unchanged. The diff touches only valid_ref_name (template/mod.rs:159), wire::ReasonCode (wire.rs:79-93) and tests; resolve/freeze logic and the digest field set are byte-identical, so every digest and refusal test passes unchanged.

2. Future-template slot typing: still latent and still unaddressed here. The new ref_name bound does harden StepId/ControlId only; a non-principal SlotKind::Policy|Observation|Artifact|Selector slot other than read is still raw WireText. This is the next template's problem, and INV-37 is still keyed on the literal slot name read.

3. Digest scope for the compiled template: unchanged and still matching plan section 8 / the ADR. No template-content digest was added.

4. Precedence nuance (duplicate property slot -> INPUT_AMBIGUOUS rather than SLOT_CONFLICT): unchanged, still the documented behaviour, and the existing test asserts it. No F-38/M1.6.4 test added that would read the code narrowly.

5. Templates::resolve_in remains private, so the generic INV-37 guard is still only exercisable in-crate; no test-only constructor was added.

One addition relevant to observation 2: the new tests now read schemas/claim-template.v1.schema.json and compare the Rust matchers with $defs/ref_name and $defs/reason_code over a candidate matrix, so the next template's slot typing can use the same fixture-driven pattern instead of a hand-copied check.

Evidence: 37 template tests (31 preserved + 6 new), 53 scourge-core lib tests, 120 scourge-verify tests, independent schema-differential matrix 63/63, cargo fmt/clippy/doc, full just check exit 0.

Leaving this thread open as a record for M1.5/M1.6; retargeted review is cr-ifws6e at 143d4ce.
